rationale: Definitions, including 'prescribed' as prescribed by rules; touches the rule-making link but says nothing about the application fee.
First and second appeals under the RTI Act; unrelated to the application fee.
Section 6(1) requires an RTI request to be accompanied by such fee as may be prescribed; the fee requirement, though the amount is left to the rules.
Sets further fees for providing information, requires fees to be reasonable, exempts below-poverty-line applicants and makes information free when time limits are missed.
The fee amount is fixed by the Right to Information Rules, 2012, which are subordinate rules not indexed.
Bars civil courts from entertaining suits about directions under the Act; related to challenging directions but does not give the NGT appeal route.
Powers of entry and inspection; not about appealing against directions.
Appeal from Central Consumer Protection Authority orders to the National Commission; a different Act and forum, and torn with 1 so graded lower.
Appeals under the RTI Act; unrelated to NGT appeals against environmental directions.
Gives any person aggrieved by a direction under section 5 an appeal to the National Green Tribunal.
The Central Government's power to issue directions, which are the orders appealable to the NGT.
Section 18 of the RTI Act, not of RERA.
Section 18 of the Environment Act, not of RERA.
Section 18 of the POSH Act, not of RERA.
Section 18 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, not of RERA.
Section 18 of the Copyright Act, not of RERA.
Section 18 of the FCRA, not of RERA.
Section 18 of the Disabilities Act, not of RERA.
Section 18 of the Consumer Protection Act, not of RERA.
Section 18 of the Contract Act, not of RERA.
The cited RERA section 18 on return of amount and compensation.
Functions and duties of promoters; does not deal with registration of real estate agents.
Bars real estate agents from facilitating sales without registration and sets the application, grant, validity and revocation procedure.
Duties of agents registered under section 9; companion obligations that follow registration.
Penalty for an agent's failure to register or contravention of sections 9 and 10.
Government power to call for information and inspect records on sexual harassment; not the committee's inquiry timeline or procedure.
Sets how the Internal Committee inquires into a complaint, its civil-court powers, and that the inquiry must be completed within ninety days.
Requires the inquiry report within ten days of completion and sets the recommendations and 60-day action by the employer.
Complaint of sexual harassment to the committee, the step that starts the inquiry.
Protection of action taken in good faith; nothing about the CCPA's powers against advertisements.
CCPA power to order recall and discontinuation of unfair trade practices; a related enforcement power but not specific to misleading advertisements.
Empowers the CCPA to direct discontinuation or modification of false or misleading advertisements, impose penalties and bar endorsers.
General CCPA functions, including ensuring no false or misleading advertisement is made or published.
Criminal punishment for false or misleading advertisement; the companion penalty.
Regulation-making power of NALSA; a rule-making provision, not its functions.
Procedure of Permanent Lok Adalats; not NALSA's functions.
Rule-making power on seafarer certificates; unrelated.
Authentication of electronic records; unrelated.
Rule-making power under the Food Security Act; unrelated.
Constitutes NALSA to exercise the Central Authority's powers and functions and sets its composition, but does not list the functions.
Requires NALSA to discharge its functions in coordination with other agencies; part of how it performs its functions.
Section 4 (Functions of the Central Authority) directly lists NALSA's functions but is not admitted.
Age-appropriate admission and special training for out-of-school children under the RTE Act; on admission but not the 25% quota.
Five per cent reservation for persons with disabilities in higher education; a different Act and level, torn with 1 so graded lower.
Inclusive education duties for children with disabilities; not the RTE 25% private-school quota.
Section 12(1)(c) requires unaided and specified schools to admit at least 25% of class I from weaker and disadvantaged children, with reimbursement under 12(2).
